<SinceRelease version="2.27.0" product="tsdb" />

<Experimental />

When you enable `timescaledb.enable_cagg_rewrites`, {C.TIMESCALE_DB} can transparently rewrite a query against a {C.HYPERTABLE} to read from a matching {C.CAGG} instead. If a {C.CAGG} aggregates exactly the columns and time buckets the query asks for, {C.TIMESCALE_DB} replaces the {C.HYPERTABLE} scan with a {C.CAGG} scan, which is much faster on large datasets.

## How {C.CAGG} query rewrites work

When you query a {C.HYPERTABLE} with `SELECT … GROUP BY time_bucket(…)`, {C.TIMESCALE_DB} looks for a {C.CAGG} on that {C.HYPERTABLE} whose definition matches the query's grouping columns, `time_bucket` width, and aggregates. If one matches, the planner replaces the {C.HYPERTABLE} scan with a scan of the {C.CAGG}'s materialization — the rewrite is invisible to the application.

The match must be exact. {C.TIMESCALE_DB} does not reaggregate (for example, it does not roll up 1-hour {C.CAGG} buckets into 2-hour query buckets).

## Use {C.CAGG} query rewrites

Turn the rewriting on:

```sql
SET timescaledb.enable_cagg_rewrites = on;
```

A second setting controls diagnostics:

```sql
SET timescaledb.cagg_rewrites_debug_info = on;
```

With `cagg_rewrites_debug_info` on, {C.TIMESCALE_DB} prints whether each query is eligible for rewriting and, if not, why. Set this on while `enable_cagg_rewrites` is off to inspect which queries would be rewritten without changing plans.

## Limitations

- **Exact match required.** The query must aggregate the same columns with the same `time_bucket` width as the target {C.CAGG}. {C.TIMESCALE_DB} does not roll up smaller buckets into larger ones to match a query.
- **Real-time {C.CAGG}s only.** A {C.CAGG} with the default `timescaledb.materialized_only = true` is not eligible. Set `materialized_only = false` on the {C.CAGG} you want the rewriter to use.
- **{C.PG} 16 or later.** Rewrites are not supported on {C.PG} 15.
